security.writes.hint: Off by default — this is the master arming switch; writing to real hardware is irreversible. When on, any device that is not write-locked can be written: declared registers use their template encoding and enforce whatever guards you declared (min/max/allowed — each guard you declare buys enforcement and a better write dialog), and undeclared registers accept a raw write after an explicit unguarded acknowledgement. devices.unit.providesHint: Fields this source supplies right now / fields selected from it

plant.wizard.idHint: a-z 0-9 - _ · in topics and device names, fixed after creation
plant.wizard.waysQ: How do we reach the datalogger?
plant.wizard.bothHint: Solar API answers in milliseconds with the essentials; Modbus (SunSpec) is slow but complete. Read both: the fast one owns the fields it offers, Modbus fills in the rest.
plant.wizard.httpHint: Fast and gentle on the datalogger; power, voltages, currents, energy — no per-string or event data.
plant.wizard.modbusHint: Complete (SunSpec), but this datalogger serves one client slowly — count on ~2 s per read.
plant.wizard.asking: Asking the datalogger what it holds…
plant.wizard.holdsIntro: An installation is not one kind of thing: its inverters, the site balance, the meter at the grid. Each is a group, totalled on its own.
plant.wizard.notAsked: The datalogger did not answer, so nothing could be found — add what it holds by hand.
plant.wizard.meterHint: Unticked on purpose: grid data is better read straight from the meter (RTU) than through the datalogger.
plant.wizard.tplHint: Templates for this kind of unit and the way it is reached come first; the others are under "Other kinds", and templates that declare no kind are listed apart.
plant.wizard.needGroup: Tick or add at least one group.
plant.wizard.readIntro: How often each group is read. Solar API is cheap; Modbus on this datalogger is not — the measured floor is shown where it matters.
plant.wizard.loadIntro: To the datalogger, this installation alone:
plant.wizard.loadOver: more than it is known to sustain (≈ {h}/min Solar API, ≈ {m}/min Modbus); read less often.
plant.wizard.precedence: Solar API (fast, partial) goes first and Modbus fills in the rest. If the Solar API goes quiet for

endpoints.srcTplHint: Maps for this kind of unit and this way of reading come first; the others are under "Other kinds".
endpoints.srcIvHint: Leave a field empty and this source will not read that kind of measurement — another source may.
endpoints.srcStaleHint2: How long its values stay authoritative before a later source may fill in. 0 = never — right for a counter.
endpoints.groupTplHint: The map for this kind of unit (offered first; other kinds are under "Other kinds") — used by any source of the group that declares none of its own.
endpoints.srcIntro: A source is one way of reaching the SAME units. Its position in the list is its precedence: the first source offering a field supplies it.
endpoints.groupIntro: A group is one kind of thing this installation holds — its inverters, the site balance, the meter at its grid connection. Groups are totalled separately.
commands.groupHint: Tell the units of this group something — a power limit, a restore. Every command is verified and audited.
commands.title: Command
commands.intro: The gateway writes the registers the template declares for this command, reads back and says whether it took. Test shows the exact registers without writing.
commands.testHint: Reads the device and shows what would be written — nothing is written.
commands.v.mismatch: written, but the device holds another value
commands.groupAcceptsHint: Offered by the template of the source that writes (Modbus, else MQTT). A ticked command can be run from this page, over MQTT and from Home Assistant; an unticked one is refused everywhere.
commands.unitIntro: What this unit can be told. Each command writes what its template declares — Modbus registers, or a value published over MQTT — then reads back and says whether it took. The same commands are accepted over MQTT and from Home Assistant; every run is audited.
commands.none: This unit's template declares no commands.
commands.enableHint: Tick it under Commands in the group editor of the installation.
commands.noHistory: Nothing yet. Every command — from this page, the API, MQTT or Home Assistant — is recorded here.
rules.import.wasArmed: armed in the file — arrives in shadow
rules.import.doneDetail: {n} of {m} imported — in shadow until you arm them
rules.import.empty: Paste the YAML or open a file first.
rules.import.replaceLabel: Replace rules that already exist here (never an armed one)
rules.import.intro: Paste a rules file exported from a gateway (Rules → Export) or written by hand. Each rule is checked against THIS installation first — its target device and command must exist here. Imported rules always arrive in shadow: they decide and say so, but write nothing until you arm them.
rules.import.title: Import rules
rules.intro: A rule decides when a command runs: it watches live values, waits for them to settle, and asks a device for what it wants. A new rule runs in shadow — it decides and says so, but writes nothing — until you arm it.
rules.none: No rules yet. A rule watches live values and asks a device for what it wants — an over-voltage limit, a restore when the grid is gone. Add one; it starts in shadow.
rules.in.noDevice: {ref}: there is no device or installation {dev}
rules.notOfferedLine: Its target no longer offers {command}: the rule cannot run until it does. Enable the command on the device, or pick another target.
rules.notOfferedNew: This example's target does not offer {command} here: enable the command on the device, or pick another target.
rules.emptyTitle: Nothing here offers a command yet
rules.emptyBody: A rule asks a device or a group for something through an enabled command. Enable one on a device's Commands tab (or an installation group's), then add the rule.
rules.savedInputsTitle: Saved — it reads names this gateway does not have
rules.import.inputsTitle: Some imported rules read names this gateway does not have
rules.clampHint: A ceiling on what the rule may ask for, for a stated time
rules.overrideHint: Pause the rule so you or another system can command its target
rules.label: Name
opcua.title: OPC UA server
opcua.intro: SCADA systems and HMI panels with an OPC UA client read every device and value of the gateway here, with its quality (Good / Uncertain) and the time it was read. Admin and operator accounts also run the devices' enabled commands (set points and methods). Off by default.
opcua.encOptional: Optional (also without — older panels; passwords travel in clear)
opcua.anonymousHint: Otherwise clients log in with the gateway's own accounts (admin, operator, viewer); five wrong passwords lock a name for five minutes.
opcua.publicHint: Empty for one gateway. For a high-availability pair behind HAProxy: the balancer's address, told to clients; the server still listens on its own port, and both gateways use one certificate (the standby takes it with the configuration).
opcua.certHint: for clients that check the server (UaExpert, Ignition, panels).
opcua.noAccounts: no accounts: turn on login, or allow anonymous
seq.title: Sequences
seq.intro: Commands in order, with waits and checks — undone in reverse when a step fails or you cancel. Each command meets every gate of a command; a safety rule holding a device still stops it.
seq.editHint: Steps: command {device, name, params}, wait_s, wait_until (with timeout_s), check (else: abort | continue). on_abort: commands that undo, run in order when a step fails or the run is cancelled.
seq.none: No sequences yet. A sequence runs commands in order — open a valve, wait until it is open, start the pump — and undoes them if a step fails.
seq.undo: If it fails or is cancelled
rules.layerHint: Several rules may drive one target: the higher priority wins it
rules.layerFieldHint: When several rules drive one target, the higher layer wins; a rule with no opinion lets the next one act.
rules.yieldsHint: Another rule drives this target now; this one writes nothing until it wins again
rules.schedHint: Days: Mon-Fri, Sat,Sun, 1-5 (1 = Monday) or all. The last entry already reached is in force, looking back up to a week.
rules.schedWhenHint: While it is false the rule asks for the off value (under Timers).
rules.forceHint: Ask for a value for a while (run for an hour), then the rule decides again
rules.todayHint: Run time and starts today (local time); in shadow, what it would have done
rules.timers: Timers: wait, minimum run and stop, maximum run, starts per hour
rules.forSHint: A change must be wanted this long, e.g. 300 = "for 5 minutes".
rules.maxOnHint: Then it stops and rests for the minimum stop.
rules.offHint: What the command asks for when the target is stopped (e.g. 0). Empty: a condition takes "False asks for", steps take "Normal".
rules.timersHint: 0 = off. A stale signal asking for the safe values never waits for a timer.
rules.timeHint: Time: hour(), weekday() (1 = Monday), between("10:00", "16:00"); counters: run_today_h("rule-id"), starts_today("rule-id").
rules.trimSignalHint: Write it so that more means "more of the value": export as a positive number, for example.
rules.trimGainHint: Proportional: gain × the distance past the threshold, at most the step. Empty = always the step.
rules.trimOffHint: Asked for under min (e.g. 0 = stop); from off it starts again at "Start at".
rules.targetHint: A group applies the command to every unit; a unit, to that one. Only targets with an enabled command are listed.
rules.signalHint: An expression over live values, written device.register — the same grammar as calculated registers (min, max, avg, abs, + - * /).
rules.stepsHint: The highest matching step wins. An immediate step skips the debounce — the emergency path.
rules.validHint: A sample outside it is ignored as sensor garbage. A change larger than the max step is held until the next sample confirms it — a one-sample artefact never reaches a step.
rules.validStepLabel: largest plausible change between two samples
rules.paramsHint: Fixed parameters of the command, name=value.
rules.staleValue: ask for a fixed value (fail closed)
rules.holdLeave: leave the device as it is
rules.previewHint: What the rule would see and want right now, nothing kept.
rules.newShadow: A new rule is saved in shadow: it decides and says so, but writes nothing until you arm it.

vmeter.title: Virtual Meters
vmeter.pageIntro: Serve a device's live values as a standard Modbus meter so other systems read them natively (EM24 → Victron grid meter, Fronius Smart Meter → DataManager).
vmeter.pageIntroBold: Enable only to validate in parallel with the real meter
vmeter.staleAfterLbl: Stale after (s) — source older than this stops the meter (fail-safe)
vmeter.refreshIntervalLbl: Refresh interval (s) — how often the meter re-samples the source (e.g. 0.25)
vmeter.onStaleLegacy: legacy — one watchdog for the whole meter (single-source default)
vmeter.onStaleFail: fail — refuse reads touching a stale register (Modbus exception)
vmeter.onStaleSentinel: sentinel — serve SunSpec N/A (float NaN, int 0x8000…)
vmeter.onStaleHold: hold — keep last value up to a cap, then fail
vmeter.portWarn: Changing the port or unit restarts the meter and briefly drops connected consumers (Victron / Fronius fall back to their own grid-loss fail-safe).
vmeter.startsDisabled2: — enable it from its card when ready (control-critical: it can feed an ESS).
vmeter.delete.body: It stops and is removed. Any connected consumer (Victron / Fronius) drops to its own grid-loss fail-safe.
vmeter.noFreePort: No free port in range — widen VMETER_PORT_END.
vmeter.needTemplate: No virtual meters yet. A virtual meter serves a register map you define: first create one on the Templates tab (which registers, from which device values), then come back and use “Add instance”.
vmeter.noneConfigured: No virtual meters configured. Use “Add instance”.
vmeter.staleTip: source stale — meter stopped responding (consumer fail-safe)
vmeter.downTip: enabled but not serving — crashed or failed to start
general.phaseRst: Classic RST — red / yellow / blue (collides with alarm colors!)
endpoints.wireHint: The bus as the tap hears it: valid frames, CRC errors, frames with no partner, bytes skipped to realign. On a healthy bus CRC errors and orphans stay at 0.
endpoints.totals.title: How the totals are made
endpoints.totals.name: Total
endpoints.totals.none: No totals declared by the template — add your own.
endpoints.totals.hint: A total you define replaces the template’s total of the same name. It is computed over the fresh units and published with the other totals (MQTT and InfluxDB).
endpoints.influx.title: InfluxDB — tags and extra outputs
endpoints.outputs.title: The totals are also written to
endpoints.outputs.none: Only the default measurement. Add an output when a consumer reads the totals under a measurement and field names of its own.
endpoints.influx.tagsHint: Written on every point of every unit, raw and calculated. ${unit_id}, ${endpoint_id} and ${device_id} are substituted per unit. A tag is part of a series’ identity: changing one starts a new series.
endpoints.totals.fromHint: Every checked field of every fresh unit goes into one pool, then the operation runs over it.
endpoints.outputs.hint: One point per cycle with every field whose total exists. ${endpoint_id} is substituted in the bucket and tag values. Empty bucket = the installation’s.
endpoints.outputs.confirmDelete: Nothing more is written to it. Its history stays in InfluxDB.
endpoints.tapHint: Listen-only: the gateway never transmits — the bus's own master sets the rhythm. One process per port.
devices.wizard.tapLocal: A serial port on this host
devices.wizard.tapWhereHint: Through a bridge, the gateway reads the bridge’s port and never writes to it. Only transparent bridges and the MBG serial bridge pass the bus’s traffic on — a Modbus TCP gateway only answers questions. The line settings are the bus’s, set on the bridge.
devices.wizard.rtuTapNetNote: Listen-only through the bridge: another master already polls this bus — the gateway never transmits, it decodes the answers that unit gives, at the master’s rhythm. Several taps can listen to one bus, each with its own unit id; a bus is either polled or tapped. After saving, Test on the device shows what the tap hears.
bridges.tappedHint: Another master polls this bus; the gateway only listens. Scan, Check mode and polled devices are off here — they would transmit.
probe.unitTip: Another slave on the same bus: asked through this device's connection, taking turns
bridges.monitorHint: Diagnostics, this bus only: every question and answer on the wire, and the register probe for any unit on it
bridges.findLead: Not sure of its IP or port? Find bridges on the LAN
bridges.findLead2: Looks at every address of the range for the ports each kind of bridge declares: our serial bridge answers its /health; a converter only has an open port, so one register is asked of a unit, as RTU and as Modbus TCP, to tell transparent from gateway. Bridges already added are not knocked on.
bridges.finding: Searching… a /24 takes a few seconds.
bridges.findNone.one: Nothing found at 1 address. A converter may use another port: add it by hand with the port from its web page.
bridges.findNone.other: Nothing found in {n} addresses. A converter may use another port: add it by hand with the port from its web page.
vmeter.whyNoTpl: An instance serves a template — create one first.
vmeter.whyAllUsed: Every template already has an instance — each instance serves its own template; create another one.
vmeter.srcInstance2: The instance's own device — follows the device each instance binds (values previewed from {dev})
templates.noneLead: No device maps yet. A map (template) says which registers a device has and how to read them — every device uses one.
devices.wizard.protoModbusOnly: A Modbus device can move between Modbus TCP, RTU, over the network or listen-only — its register map stays valid. HTTP and MQTT read by path, so they need a new device.
devices.wizard.gwDirect: Directly — its own IP and port
devices.wizard.gwHint: An RS-485 slave behind a converter in “Modbus TCP to RTU” mode: pick the gateway, then the slave’s unit ID. The gateway’s address and connection limit come from the bridge.
adv.title: Advanced
adv.summary: calculated fields, commands, display, scan recognition, setup, notes, rule examples, details, raw JSON
adv.noProblems: No problems — Save to keep it.
adv.calc.lead: A value the device does not report, computed from the ones it does — total power from the three phases, a power factor, a status decoded to text. Every device made from this template gets it; it publishes to MQTT and InfluxDB like a register.
adv.calc.exHint: A formula reads the registers of the same device by their name. Functions: min, max, avg, abs, round, sqrt, pow, floor, ceil, clamp, popcount; prev(x) and dt for rates.
adv.calc.nameHint: Letters, digits and _ — not the name of a register.
adv.calc.moreSum: text states, MQTT topic, totals of an installation, dashboard
adv.calc.enumHint: One “code = text” per line: the computed number is published as the text.
adv.calc.topicHint: Relative to the device topic. Empty: the name.
adv.agg.title: Totals of an installation
adv.agg.hint: When several units of this template form an installation (a battery bank, an inverter farm), each line publishes one total: its name and how the units’ values combine. pack_average_soc = average of soc.
adv.cmd.lead: A named, guarded write — “power_limit = 60 %” — that a controller, a rule, Home Assistant or the UI can ask for, without knowing the registers. The template says how: which registers, in which order, what must be true first, and how to check it took.
adv.cmd.exHint: A value is a number, ${param}, or a small JSON rule: {"*": ["${value}", 10]} multiplies, {"if": "${value} < 100", "then": 1, "else": 0} chooses.
adv.cmd.name: Name
adv.cmd.nameHint: a-z 0-9 _ - · it becomes an MQTT topic and an HA entity
adv.cmd.confirm: Ask for confirmation in the UI
adv.cmd.isAlias: A shortcut for another command with fixed parameters (e.g. “restore” = power_limit 100 %)
adv.cmd.paramsHint: What the caller gives. The main one is called “value” (Home Assistant shows it as a number). Bounds are enforced before anything is written.
adv.cmd.guardHint: Registers read before writing; if one does not hold, nothing is written. Fill one condition per line.
adv.cmd.writesHint: Modbus: consecutive registers go out as one frame. MQTT: each is published on its row’s write topic. A value: a number, ${value}, or a JSON rule.
adv.cmd.verifyHint: Read back after the settle time; a difference beyond the tolerance answers “mismatch”.
adv.cmd.settleHint: Modbus: wait before verifying. MQTT: the longest wait for the read-back.
adv.cmd.readbackHint: So MQTT/HA see the new value in seconds.
adv.cmd.safeHint: The parameters a timed (leased) command is restored with when its lease expires — e.g. value = 100 % for a power limit.
adv.disp.lead: How a unit of this kind is shown — read live from the template, so improving it reaches every existing unit. Without it the UI uses sensible defaults; declare only what you want different.
adv.disp.glanceHint: In its installation and the device list · up to 12, comma-separated.
adv.disp.heroHint: The first three show · up to 12.
adv.disp.headline: Headline of an installation
adv.disp.headlineHint: Its top line, from its TOTALS (see Totals of an installation on each row) · up to 6.
adv.disp.alarmsHint: A field that is non-zero when something is wrong; it counts on the fleet and the installation, and shows on the unit.
adv.disp.sectionsHint: A category shown as a grid of tiles (cell voltages) or only its active rows (alarms). Tiles: a pattern of field names, e.g. ^cell_\d+$.
adv.disp.bitmasksHint: A field whose bits each mean one thing (balancing cells): shown as the list of what is set. The label carries {n} for the bit number.
adv.idf.lead: How a bus scan recognises this device: registers that must read given values (a model code, a fixed marker), and/or what the device says about itself (Modbus identification, FC43). When a scan finds a slave that matches, it proposes this template.
adv.idf.exHint: Every register line must hold. FC43 fields are patterns (regular expressions) on the vendor and product names the device reports.
adv.det.lead: Who made this map, from what, and how its measurements are grouped. Categories decide the sections of a device page and their order.
adv.det.versionHint: Raise it when you change the map: devices made from it are offered the update.
adv.det.author: Author
adv.det.catsHint: Each row of the map names one. Renaming one renames it on its rows; one still used cannot be deleted.
adv.json.lead: The whole template as JSON, for what is quicker typed than clicked — or pasted from a colleague. Apply puts it into the editor (nothing is saved until Save); Check shows what a save would refuse.
adv.json.noRegs: a template object with a “registers” list
adv.row.lead: What this row carries beyond its address and type. Everything is optional.
adv.row.descriptionHint: Shown where the row is picked.
adv.row.accessHint: Informative; writing is allowed by “Wr” on the row.
adv.row.scaleFromHint: SunSpec style: another register holds the power of ten (value × 10^SF). The fixed scale then divides after it.
adv.row.nanHint: “true”: the type’s standard marker (0x8000, 0xFFFF…); or the raw value(s). Such a reading is missing, not data.
adv.row.counterHint: A growing counter ignores a reading that goes backwards (a glitch would look like a reset to Home Assistant and InfluxDB). A day counter keeps the day’s maximum and adopts only the midnight reset.
adv.row.allowed: Only these values may be written
adv.row.allowedHint: Comma-separated; Home Assistant offers them as a list.
adv.row.haHint: Empty: guessed from the unit. Set them when the guess is wrong.
adv.row.title: Row details: description, not-available marker, counters, scale factor, totals, Home Assistant
devices.wizard.udp: Over UDP (datagrams instead of a connection)
devices.wizard.udpHint: Some devices and gateways answer Modbus TCP frames in UDP datagrams (usually port 502) instead of a TCP connection. Use it only when the manual says UDP.
devices.wizard.framingHint: RTU (binary, CRC) is what almost every device speaks. ASCII (“:” … LRC, readable hex) is found on older PLCs and meters — use it only when the manual says Modbus ASCII. All slaves on one line speak the same one.
adv.setup.lead: Words the gateway writes to the device before part of its map exists — some interfaces show extra values only once told which ones. Written at connect, again after the device comes back from an outage, and again when a register a step provides is refused as an illegal address (the device forgot). One write-multiple frame per step; only where writes are allowed.
adv.setup.exHint: Values are 16-bit words: decimal, or hex like 0x8238. Declare the rows of the registers a step provides like any other row.
adv.setup.name: Name
adv.setup.valuesHint: Comma or line separated; decimal or 0x… (at most 123).
adv.setup.provHint: A refusal there means the device forgot: the step is written again.
devtpl.writeGapHint: For interfaces that relay writes slowly and choke on a burst (e.g. 2). 0 = none.
devtpl.singleWritesHint: For devices that refuse FC16: every write goes out as one FC6 per register, in order.
adv.cmd.refreshHint: For a setting the device forgets by itself: the last parameters are written again until the safe ones are sent. 0 = off.
commands.refreshingHint: The device forgets this setting by itself: it is written again until the safe value is sent.
commands.enableHintDevice: Test shows what it would write without writing. Tick “Enabled on this device” to allow Run, the API and MQTT.
tplNotes.hasWarning: This template has a note to read
adv.notes.lead: What a user should know before relying on this template: a model it does not fit, a value the device leaves at 0, a step to take first. Shown when the template is picked and at the top of every device made from it; a warning that names a command or a field marks it where it is listed.
adv.notes.fieldsHint: Commands or fields this note is about, comma separated — they get a mark where they are listed.
adv.calc.categoryHint: Where it is listed — and its InfluxDB measurement when nothing else names one.
adv.rules.lead: Rules a device of this kind is commonly run with. They are examples: the rule editor offers them under "Start from" for every device made from this template, with {device} replaced by its id, and a rule always starts in shadow. Each is a rule as in the rules guide; its command must be one of this template's and the fields it reads must be its own.
rules.presetHint: Examples from the templates of your devices. A rule always starts in shadow: it decides and logs, it writes nothing until you arm it.
rules.untilHint: Hysteresis: once "When" holds, the rule stays on "True asks for" until this holds. Empty: "False asks for" follows as soon as "When" turns false.
rules.releaseHint: Between this and the first step the rule holds what it has — the dead band.
meter.title: Electricity measured by
meter.lead: For a device with no meter of its own: name the meter on its supply. The device then shows electric power (power_electric, W) and energy (energy_electric) as its own — its Energy tab works, and its template can use them (a heat pump's COP). A device that measures itself needs nothing here.
tip.nodes: Flash ESP boards from this browser and see the nodes on the network (a separate service)
security.nodes.title: ESP nodes service
security.nodes.hint: Address of the ESP nodes service (available in MBG Pro), e.g. /nodes/ on the same host. When set, it is listed in Settings → Modules. Empty = not listed.
devices.espEncryptedTip: Native API uses encryption — identity not readable, but the device is ESPHome
tokens.title: Service tokens
tokens.hint: For programs, not people: a companion service or a script signs in with a named token (sent as Authorization: Bearer). It has a role like a login, the audit log shows its name, and revoking it touches no one's password. The token is shown once, when it is made.
tokens.name: Name (who uses it)
tokens.once: Copy it now: it is not shown again.
